tests.mutation: Applicability.Of excluded the date itself (`saleOrExchangeDate > ApplicableFrom` for `saleOrExchangeDate >= ApplicableFrom`), so a sale on 24 December 2002 was outside the section; this test went red. It went red too with Applicability.ApplicableFrom set to the corpus's pinned baseline date (`new(2026, 1, 1)` for `new(2002, 12, 24)`), with it set a day early (`new(2002, 12, 23)`), and with SectionApplicability.Authority citing exclusion-of-gain's `§ 1.121-1(a)` (`MapEntries.ExclusionOfGain.Locator` for `MapEntries.EffectiveDate.Locator`). Citing retroactive-election's locator did NOT turn it red: both entries cite `§ 1.121-1(f)`, so the locator cannot tell them apart.

Applicability.Of found every sale within the section (`true` for `saleOrExchangeDate >= ApplicableFrom`); this test went red. It went red too with Applicability.ApplicableFrom a day early (`new(2002, 12, 23)` for `new(2002, 12, 24)`), with the finding recording the rule's date instead of the caller's (`new SectionApplicability(ApplicableFrom, ...` for `new SectionApplicability(saleOrExchangeDate, ...`), and with Authority citing exclusion-of-gain's `§ 1.121-1(a)`.

Handlers.EffectiveDate defaulted a missing date to the effective date (`request.SaleOrExchangeDate ?? Applicability.ApplicableFrom` for `Demand(request.SaleOrExchangeDate, ...)`), so a request with no date resolved as within the section; this test went red. It went red too with a missing date answered as an unresolved `MissingRulesData` decline citing `§ 1.121-1(f)` instead of refused.

Handlers.EffectiveDate defaulted a missing date to the effective date (`request.SaleOrExchangeDate ?? Applicability.ApplicableFrom` for `Demand(request.SaleOrExchangeDate, ...)`), so `Registry.Resolve("effective-date", RuleRequest.Empty)` resolved as within the section; this test went red. It went red too with a missing date answered as an unresolved `MissingRulesData` decline instead of refused.
